boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Smithfield Crossing record (August 25-29, 1864) in Sheridan's Valley Campaign [August-October 1864]. Within the frozen interval, the August 25 cavalry fight near Kearneysville, the August 26 reconnaissance at Halltown and the August 28 fight at Leetown and Smithfield are recorded separately in the sources and are not added to the August 29 engagement. Campaign-wide marches, destruction, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions; the live field reads zero. NPS, Sheridan and Pond say two Confederate infantry divisions (Sheridan adds a small cavalry force) drove Merritt's division from Smithfield on August 29 until Ricketts's division came up. For August 25 Pond says Torbert's troopers faced four infantry divisions, Breckinridge's corps being the only force much engaged.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications only; no counts. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Sheridan says he reinforced Merritt's cavalry with Ricketts's division, which drove the enemy back over the Opequon; Pond says Ricketts was hurried to Merritt's relief. For August 25 Sheridan names Torbert as in command. The frozen commanders are Lieutenant General Early and Brigadier General Wesley Merritt; the live page gives Early as Major General.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report and a history; neither listed commander receives automatic sole credit, and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 300 total; the live field reads 300 (US 100; CS 200). Pond gives the August 29 loss of Gibbs's brigade as 35 killed and wounded; Sheridan says of August 28 that his loss was not very heavy. Pond's August 26 figures at Halltown (Crook's infantry 141) and the unnumbered August 25 losses are separate actions and are not added.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Merritt's and Torbert's reports, Ricketts's report, Sheridan's August 25-27 dispatches (read, not selected), Hotchkiss's journal and the Confederate reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes Sheridan's, Torbert's, Wright's and Early's reports and despatches and is not independent of them. Sheridan's dispatches of August-September 1864 and his report dated New Orleans, February 3, 1866 are one family of interested Union accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XLIII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
